newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares fall at noon in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares fall at noon in cautious trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index fell slightly during the Thursday morning session, with investors cautious about trading in the early stages of the corporate interim reporting season, brokers said.
The index edged down 0.53 points or 0.39 percent to 132.81 points on thin turnover of HK$12 million.
"Investors are still adopting a wait-and-see attitude," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
Listed firms must announce their 1997 interim results by August 31, but none of the 49 Shenzhen-listed B share companies have yet to do so.
"The B share market will continue tight-band correction with limited downsides," a stock analyst at the Hainan Province Trust and Investment Co said.
The domestic A share index shed 3.84 points or 0.91 percent to 417.37 points in turnover of 2.4 billion yuan.

Brokers said the falls were triggered by the poor performance of market leader Shenzhen Development Bank, which fell 1.11 yuan to 35.86 yuan on the morning's second most active trade of 7.5 million shares.
Investors sold the bank's shares because they were disappointed with its 1997 earnings outlook, the brokers said.
On the B share market, retailer Shenzhen International Enterprise was the worst performer, sliding HK$0.21 or 5.40 percent to HK$3.68.
